user.title: Connect to PeekESP
user.description:
Enter the pairing code your device shows on screen. Dashes and capitals do not matter.

The code never leaves Home Assistant — the stream id and access tokens are derived from it here, and neither can be turned back into the code.

data_description.pair_code: Ten characters, as shown on the device. For example K7M2-P4QX-9R.
data_description.name: What to call this in Home Assistant.
data_description.relay: Only change this if you deployed your own Cloudflare Worker.

reauth_confirm.title: Pairing code changed
reauth_confirm.description: The relay no longer accepts the stored code. This happens when a new code is generated on the device, or after re-flashing with --erase. Enter the code now shown on screen.

error.invalid_code: That is not a valid pairing code. It is ten characters, and the letters I and O and the digits 0 and 1 are never used.
error.already_claimed: Another reader already holds this stream. Either someone else has this pairing code, or the device has since generated a new one.
error.timeout: The relay did not answer in time.
error.insecure_relay: The relay URL must start with https://.
error.unknown: Unexpected error. Check the Home Assistant log for details.

abort.already_configured: That pairing code is already set up.

init.title: PeekESP options
init.description: How often to poll the relay. Every reader shares one request budget: at 30 seconds this costs about 2,880 requests a day against Cloudflare's free 100,000, and each agent and each display costs 17,280 of it at their 5-second default.
